description: InsarViz is a Python tool for interactively exploring large satellite interferometry datasets. The JOSS paper says it is designed for deformation of ground and man-made structures, where standard image viewers are insufficient. The software’s own Zenodo record identifies the package and states GPL-3.0; the linked university GitLab site displayed a bot-check page and was not opened. Spatial coverage is the supplied InSAR footprint, and temporal coverage is its satellite acquisitions. Deformation time series can help inspect movement near buildings, roads or other assets and calibrate ground-motion exposure simulations. A caveat is that line-of-sight satellite motion is not a direct structural-damage measure. Atmospheric effects, reference choice and viewing geometry require separate checks. No matching catalogue or first-review software record was found. The article and Zenodo metadata were read without downloading its software archive or attempting the GitLab challenge.
name: InsarViz satellite-deformation analysis
